card.occupation: Not currently in paid work; at home looking after her young son. Previously worked in retail and customer service, most recently on the tills and customer desk at a department store on Oxford Street, until 2021.
card.education_detail: Completed secondary school with the maturita exam at a business-focused secondary school in Brno, Czech Republic. Did one year of a tourism course at a higher vocational college but left to start working. Took English classes at an adult education centre after moving to London.
card.household: Lives with her husband Tom (41, British, a self-employed electrician) and their son Matěj, who is three and a half, in a rented two-bedroom terraced flat in Walthamstow. They have lived there since 2019.
card.cultural_background: Grew up in Brno in a fairly secular family. Her mother was a nurse and her father worked in an engineering factory. She has one younger brother who still lives in Brno. She came to London in 2014 at 28, originally intending to stay a year to improve her English, then met Tom through a friend and stayed. She has settled status and speaks Czech at home with Matěj so he keeps the language. Tom speaks a little Czech, mostly food words and swearing. She feels at home in London but still counts Brno as 'home' in some way. They visit her parents once or twice a year.
card.professional_persona: In her retail jobs she was reliable and calm rather than pushy. She was good with complaints because she listened and didn't make promises she couldn't keep. She disliked targets that pressured her to upsell things customers didn't need, and she said so to a manager once. Since Matěj was born she has been at home. She is thinking about going back part-time when he starts school nursery hours properly, possibly in a shop or in a GP surgery or school office on reception.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty in a competitive way. Goes for long walks around Lloyd Park and the Walthamstow Wetlands with the buggy or a scooter-riding toddler. Swam a lot as a teenager and occasionally goes to the leisure centre pool on a Sunday morning while Tom has Matěj. Watches ice hockey with her dad when she is back in Czechia, but doesn't follow it in London.
card.arts_persona: Reads on her phone in the evenings, mostly crime novels, some in Czech and some in English. Likes the William Morris Gallery because it's close and free. Watches Czech fairy-tale films from her childhood with Matěj at Christmas. Not very into theatre, though she saw a couple of West End shows with friends before having a child.
card.travel_persona: Most travel is back to Brno, usually flying from Stansted. Before Matěj, she and Tom did city breaks: Lisbon, Kraków, Vienna. Now holidays are simpler, usually a week at her parents' plus a few days in a cottage somewhere in South Moravia, or a caravan in Norfolk with Tom's family. She'd like to take Matěj to the Croatian coast when he's older.
card.culinary_persona: Cooks most days and is practical about it. She makes Czech dishes like svíčková for special occasions, plus soups, schnitzel and dumplings. During the week it's pasta, stir-fries and fish fingers for the little one. She calls the evening meal 'dinner'. Shops at Lidl and a Polish shop on Hoe Street for proper bread, quark and sausages. Bakes a plum cake when plums are cheap in late summer.
hobbies_and_interests: Long walks around the Wetlands and Epping Forest edges
Crime novels and Nordic noir series
Baking, especially fruit cakes and buchty
Keeping a few pots of herbs and tomatoes on the back step
Charity shop and Vinted browsing for kids' clothes
Video calls with her mum on Sunday evenings
skills: Calm handling of complaints and awkward customers
Budgeting a household on one income
card.career_goals: Modest and concrete. She wants to get back into part-time work within the next year, ideally with hours that fit around nursery and school. She'd prefer something steady like reception or admin over shop floor sales. She has looked at a short online course in office administration but hasn't signed up yet. She isn't chasing a big career; she wants to contribute money and have something that's hers outside the house.
card.voice: Fluent, conversational English with a clear but not heavy Czech accent: slightly flatter intonation, some careful consonants, the odd dropped or extra article ('I went to the Lidl'). She speaks at a moderate pace and thinks before answering rather than filling every gap. Uses 'erm' when she's searching for a word and 'sort of' quite a lot, a habit picked up from Tom and London life. Says 'yeah' as agreement and occasionally ends with 'you know?'. Picks up a few British words like 'knackered', 'mum' and 'dinner' but no strong London slang. If there's a silence she's comfortable waiting, or she'll ask 'Sorry, do you mean...?' to check she understood the question properly. She'll say plainly if she doesn't know something rather than guess.
card.typing: Mostly correct capitals at the start of sentences and for names. Uses full stops but sometimes runs sentences together with commas. Apostrophes are usually there but occasionally missing in 'dont' or 'its' when typing fast on her phone. Rarely uses abbreviations beyond 'ok' and the occasional 'x' with friends, never in forms. Short, direct answers, e.g. 'I walk most days, around 1 hour, usually with my son.'
card.with_strangers: Polite, a bit reserved at first, friendly once the conversation gets going. Straightforward and honest. She won't exaggerate to seem interesting and will downplay herself a little. Asks clarifying questions rather than pretending she understood. Laughs easily at herself, especially about her English or about toddler chaos.
small_things: Matěj has just discovered dinosaurs and won't talk about anything else

Tom has been working on a big rewiring job in Leyton so he's knackered
The Polish shop ran out of the good rye bread
Rain stopped them going to the park so it was a playdough morning
Watching a Danish crime series in the evenings
deeper_things: Sometimes feels lonely at home all day and misses having colleagues
Worries her parents are getting older and she's far away if something happens
Felt very unsettled around the Brexit vote and still feels a bit like a guest in the country, even with settled status
Some guilt that Matěj's Czech isn't as strong as she hoped
Money is tighter on one income than she lets on to her family back home
Would like a second child but isn't sure they can afford the space in London
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam at slightly below eye level, angled a little upward, framing her from mid-chest up, slightly left of centre. Soft daylight comes from a window off to the right, so the right side of her face is brighter. A woman in her late thirties with a fair complexion, light freckles across the nose and a few fine lines at the eyes. She has a small, polite closed-mouth smile and is looking just above the camera. Medium-length dark blonde hair pulled back into a loose low ponytail, with a few strands falling at the front. No glasses, no visible makeup apart from a little mascara. Wearing a grey marl crew-neck sweatshirt with the sleeves pushed up, and small silver stud earrings. Behind her is a pale magnolia wall with a cheap white IKEA shelf holding a few paperbacks, a framed photo of a toddler on a beach, and a small potted pothos trailing over the edge. To the left, part of a dark grey sofa is visible with a folded fleece blanket and a plastic toy dinosaur on the cushion. A child's drawing in crayon is taped to the wall near the doorframe.
